title: Offline detection
summary: The runtime's connectivity tracker decides that a device or gateway is offline from what it hears, without asking Laravel, and reports each episode once. The middle row is the decision; the top row is what holds it back. As the code stands, Laravel records and shows offline alerts and notifies nobody.

boxes.label: Heard
boxes.sub: Receipt time per device and edge
boxes.detail: Any packet counts as hearing from its source, before validation, so a rejected packet still shows the device is alive. A node packet counts for the edge node and its own device, not the devices behind it. A death counts as a death once the engine accepts it. On an adapter's edge only a DDATA with readings not marked historical counts.

boxes.label: Reporting interval
boxes.detail: Keeps up to 65 distinct observed times per device from the last 7 days and takes the median gap between check-ins. Readings less than 10 seconds apart that together span less than 10 seconds are one check-in, so a device that sends a few messages at once every two hours reports every two hours. It uses observed time, not receipt time. At start the times are seeded from stored observations, 500 devices a query. With fewer than three check-ins the device is learning and is not judged by silence.

boxes.label: Offline after
boxes.detail: Three reporting intervals plus the poll interval, rounded up to the minute and kept between 15 minutes and 7 days. The poll interval comes from the adapter's running revision, otherwise it is zero. The runtime would use a set value, but nothing in Laravel sets one yet, so every device uses this automatic one.

boxes.label: Judge on the 5 s tick
boxes.sub: Death, or silence past Offline after
boxes.detail: A device that stays connected is offline on its own death certificate, its edge node's, or when silence since its anchor passes Offline after. A device that connects to report, which every adapter-fed device is, ignores deaths. The anchor is the latest of the last packet, the runtime's start and the last broker reconnect, by receipt time. A device not heard since monitoring began is never judged.

boxes.label: Interruptions
boxes.detail: A gap on the platform's side neither opens nor clears an episode. A runtime start or a restored broker connection restarts silence from that moment and forgets deaths. An adapter's node death pauses its devices until its next node birth, and the time it was down is left out of their silence.

boxes.label: Gateway rule
boxes.detail: Such an edge is a subject of its own, owned by its connection's organization. Its node death, or the whole edge being silent past the largest threshold of the devices concerned, opens a gateway episode. Devices of another organization behind the same gateway (moved there) get a separate episode for that organization, so each alert lists only its own organization's devices. Those devices open no episode of their own while theirs is open or pending, and are judged from the gateway's return when it clears. An adapter's edge is never a gateway.

boxes.label: Grace period
boxes.detail: An episode opens only when the offline condition has held for grace_seconds (120) with no packet in between, and clears when the subject has been back that long. A device that connects to report clears at its next report. A shorter drop leaves no episode.

boxes.label: Row and outbox event
boxes.detail: An opened, cleared or stopped transition is written with its device.connectivity.v1 outbox event in one transaction, and the tracker changes its own state only after that. The event id is a UUID v5 of the subject key, episode and transition. Deactivating or removing a device stops an open episode with a reason; it does not clear it.

boxes.label: ConnectivityProjector
boxes.detail: Runs in Laravel's runtime inbox transaction. It creates a device_offline or gateway_offline alert with severity warning, the cause, offline_since, last_seen_at and the threshold used, and lists the affected devices. A hosted organization's gateway episode becomes that organization's alert, recorded only when both organizations share a billing account and every listed device is hosted on that gateway. It then writes an event-log entry with source connectivity and an audit record.

boxes.label: Shown in the portal
boxes.detail: Offline alerts appear in the Alerts inbox, where they can be acknowledged, assigned and commented on, in the Event log, and as the offline_alert status in the device list. The device page also asks the tracker for its live state (waiting, learning, monitored, pending, offline, recovering, interrupted or disabled) through GET /internal/connectivity.

boxes.label: Nobody is notified
boxes.sub: No email, bell or integration event
boxes.detail: An offline alert creates no delivery, no bell notification and no alert.*.v1 event. ConnectivityProjector calls none of them, EventJournal skips alerts that are not workflow alerts, and DeliverAlertEmail cancels a delivery for one. Recipients, mutes and per-device settings are not in the code.

steps.text: A packet arrives. Before it is validated, the tracker notes the receipt time for its device and its edge node.
The observed times of the device's readings are kept. Readings sent together count as one check-in, and the median gap between check-ins is its reporting interval.
With three check-ins the device has an Offline after: three intervals plus any poll interval, between 15 minutes and 7 days.
Every 5 seconds the tracker judges each subject: a death certificate, or silence longer than Offline after, is an offline condition.
While the broker connection is down or the device's adapter is restarting, the device is not judged, and that time does not count as silence.
If the device sits behind a gateway that is offline or going offline, the gateway gets one episode per organization with devices behind it, and the device opens none.
An offline condition must hold for two minutes. A packet in that time cancels it and leaves no alert.
Then the episode opens: the row and its device.connectivity.v1 event are written in one transaction.
The event reaches Laravel through the runtime inbox. ConnectivityProjector creates the alert, keyed so a replay changes nothing.
The alert shows in the Alerts inbox, the Event log, the device list and the device page.
That is all: no email, no bell notification and no integration event is produced for an offline alert today.
When the device has been heard again for two minutes, a cleared transition takes the same path and the alert ends.
